description: Import a parcel as the garden's site context: sets the scheme outline, geo-anchor, and (by default) auto-loads the KIEG WMS cadastral/satellite map background so `capture_preview` shows real site context (neighbors, road, vegetation) under the boundary. Default alignment is `north_up` so cardinal reasoning ("south wall", "west fence") works naturally; pass `side_aligned` if you'd rather draw on an axis-aligned canvas. WMS failure is non-fatal — boundary + geo-anchor still land and the response carries `mapBackground: { loaded: false, reason }` so you can decide whether to retry or continue without the background. Pass `loadMapBackground: false` to skip the WMS fetch entirely (faster; useful for headless evals). Poland only: refused for a garden placed outside Poland — draw the boundary with set_boundary instead.

alignment.description: Boundary orientation. `north_up` (default) keeps north pointing up; `side_aligned` rotates so the longest edge runs horizontally. The alignment modal that the editor would normally show for skewed parcels is bypassed when called via MCP.

loadMapBackground.description: Auto-load the KIEG WMS cadastral/satellite map background after import. Default `true`. Set `false` to skip the WMS fetch (faster; `capture_preview` will then show the parcel on a blank background and `get_garden_info().hasScheme` stays `false`).

parcelId.description: Parcel ID to import (use get_parcel_by_* first to find it)

name: import_parcel
